newsitem.title: UK: INSIGHT - Gilts seen consolidating, prop at 113-30.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT - Gilts seen consolidating, prop at 113-30.

text.p: British gilts look set to consolidate on Monday as the market pauses for breath after its impressive climb in the last few weeks, technical analysts said.
They said the June contract should be fairly well supported at Friday's low of 113-30, and would bump into initial resistance around 114-14,18.

"We're likely to consolidate today and see sideways movement while we look to establish direction," said London Bond Broking technical strategist Marc Ostwald. He added last week's rally was helped by investors being short and having to cover.
The June contract opened up 3/32 at 114-10.
Ostwald said a break below 113-30 would see the market heading towards 113-18, the high from last Wednesday.
"If we break that, we're into a much more serious correction and will likely fall towards 112-28 pretty quickly," he said.
Charts show the market hit a daily low of 112-28 on May 8.
On the upside, an area of congestion at 114-14,18 will restrain the market initially.

"If we can break through that we could test 114-24, the high on Friday," said Ostwald. "And longer term, if you really think it can go another point and a half, I'd expect the rally to die out around 115-24, congestion dating back to October 1993."
Juliette Clark at the Royal Bank of Scotland said a near-doji formation on candlestick charts suggested a period of volatile trading.
A doji occurs when the market opens and closes at the same level, forming a cross on candlestick charts.
"Given that the momentum indicators are nearing overbought there is a chance that this pattern is a warning sign of a major reversal, so be careful," she said in a note.
"For the moment thoough, the bulls are firmly in control."
By 0725 GMT, September short sterling was up seven basis points at 93.28.
